trick: Explain the bug before you fix it
source_quote: "Explain what's broken and how to fix it, but do not modify any files yet." (Tweag Agentic Coding Handbook, debug workflow; also: "Reason before fixing")
source_note: Approved by Sebi 4 Nov 2026 (PROTOCOL.md). Module 6 rules = private/m5/RULES.md 'Runs' section: one project (the M6 fixture, being built in parallel; base set 4 Nov from the built fixture), Haiku 4.5, 18 runs a side, three numbers recorded before each run (pass rate = all four traps D1-D4 + core from the grader's `BUGS` line, the behaviour count below, cost per passed run), the habit measured on the plain side first, an agent reads every transcript. allowed_tools_extra mirrors Module 5 and is re-aligned to the fixture's real test command before the run. Design rationale and kill switches: private/m6/DESIGN.md.
behaviour_count: Where the FIRST source edit lands: the D1 symptom file vs the root-cause file (from events), per side; plus with-side explanations hand-labelled right root cause / symptom only / wrong, and runs that edited files during the explain turn (snapshot after call 1 differs from lab-base)
habit_measure: Plain side: runs that write a root-cause statement in text before their first Edit/Write (events), and runs whose first edit is in the D1 symptom file
anchor: Asked to explain first, N of 18 named the real cause before touching code; left alone, M of 18 started editing where the bug showed, not where it was

with.label: Task + Tweag's 'explain, don't modify yet' line, then 'Now fix it.' in the same session
